first_impression: Clean deck, real recordings, a walker that cheated. Solo and 12 hours. I want to see it run live, not slides.
confusing: Slide 6 headline '3.2 days of practice' is simulated robot time, a vanity number that sounds like wall-clock work until you read the formula
Slide 10 stacks 40x, 22x, 121x, 3.7x and 32.8x, so I can't tell which number to remember
Slide 8 shows 6.16 m/s but the notes and the ablation row say 6.64; also the 'cheetah' slip row appears with no setup
doubts: 40x compares a GPU 2D impulse sim to MuJoCo 3D soft-contact on CPU; the physics is much cheaper, so it isn't a like-for-like speedup
'Same answers as the pro simulator' on slide 9: the passive-collapse height curve visibly diverges at 0.5 s, and open-loop x drifts by 15 cm
Hopper on slide 11 reaches only 3.17 m in 17 s, which looks like barely learning, and the CLI is shown for a different robot than the headline walker
Agents wrote most of the code, so how much of the Metal codegen and the PPO do you personally understand?
questions: Show the Metal kernel recompiling live when you add the fourth leg, and let me change a reward
Why no MJX or Warp number, even on CPU, as a baseline?
Does the 5-seed claim use the same reward and settings as the headline walker, and what was the worst seed?
Why is policy distance 21.9 m in MacGym versus 19.8 m in MuJoCo on slide 14 when the table says 19.7 versus 22.0? Which is correct?

fixes.change: Lead with wall-clock facts (4,096 tripods, 28 s, 3.2 sim-days) and label the 3.2 days 'simulated' in the headline itself
Cut to one headline number (22x at the 4,096 envs actually trained) and move 121x and the breakdown to the Q&A or a backup slide
Retitle to 'matches MuJoCo on analytics, tracks the walker for 0.6 s' and drop 'same answers'; reviewers will punish the overclaim
Show the walker's train run (the 54 m, 87 s fresh-install number) in the terminal instead of the weak hopper run
Make the MacGym and MuJoCo numbers the same across the bar chart and the text (21.9 vs 22.0, 19.8 vs 19.7), and put the mass +20% failure (3/20 falls) up front
Run the live L demo on stage as the climax, and trim the recording so it doesn't end on a visible SyntaxError in the console

first_impression: Gorgeous deck, suspiciously polished. A Metal-kernel RL framework in 4 hours is a big claim. Show me the repo.
confusing: Slide 12 gives hours, commits and checks but never says what a check tests; 18 passing checks is weak proof next to a 4-hour framework
Slide 14 mixes DONE and NEXT, and its dotted ghost robot art for the SO-101 arm doesn't help
Slide 7's chart axis (54.9 m up to 20 s episodes) and the lane rows (21.5 m in 8 s) use different distances, with only a small grey footnote to reconcile them
Slide 13 uses 87 s for the install path, but the headline suggests an RL class
doubts: 'Metal kernel recompiled in 0.24 s' is on a 9-body robot; does it hold for bigger robots?
The only comparison is to MuJoCo's CPU rollout; the 'no fast Mac path' claim rests on one jax-metal quote
The agents wrote most of the code; the ownership of the physics is unclear
The users are the presenter's own club and hackathons, with no outside user and no data on class adoption
questions: What is the largest robot you have compiled, and does it still run near the 6.8M steps/s?
Why does the walker plateau around 60 m, and what stops it going faster?
What breaks when you replace impulse contacts with something stiffer, and can it do 3D?
Which parts of the Metal codegen did you write or debug yourself?

fixes.change: Replace the stats row with a concrete list of the walls hit and fixed (cheating gait, contact warm-start, torque curve) and name the tests, so 'built today' reads as verified rather than generated
Plot the 8 s replay distance on the chart, or show both axes on the same scale, so the 54.9 m and 21.5 m figures don't read as inconsistent
Put an actual outside-user quote or a workshop date from the DVHS club on the slide; 'first users: me' won't convince
Show the full generated Metal kernel for a few lines side by side with the Python, and enlarge the code, which is small at the back of a room
Cut the 'next' rows (CUDA/ROCm, 3D) to one line; unbuilt claims dilute the sim-to-sim result
Say 'planar 2D' in the headline on slide 3, not as an orange sub-line, so no judge thinks you're hiding it
